newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Strike in Karachi area after five killed in attack.
newsitem.headline: Strike in Karachi area after five killed in attack.

text.p: A strike closed shops and businesses in southern parts of the Pakistani city of Karachi on Tuesday as angry residents mourned five activists of an ethnic party killed in a drive-by shooting the night before.
Witnesses said paramilitary troops patrolled the area in vans mounted with sub-machine guns. People stayed away from work and many of those on the streets wore black arm-bands.
Black flags were flying near the scene of Monday night's attack on an office of the ethnic Mohajir National Movement (MQM) in the Risala neighbourhood of District South.

Police said one of the 14 people wounded in the assault by gunmen in a yellow car had died overnight, bringing the death toll in the incident to five and the overall toll from violence in the southern port city to nine in the past 24 hours.

Irate residents of the area observed a complete strike on Tuesday and did not allow shops to open, witnesses said. The strike was also observed in the nearby areas of Burns Road, Pakistan Chowk, Ranchor Lines, Eidgah, Nanakwara and Bhimpura.
No group has claimed responsibility for the attack.

Violence has risen in the volatile port city in recent weeks amid tension between the mainstream MQM, now part of a coalition government in Sindh province, of which Karachi is the capital, and the rival MQM-Haqiqi splinter group.
Unidentified gunmen killed two MQM-Haqiqi militants in an attack on the party's headquarters, known locally as the White House, in the Landhi district on Thursday.
Four people, including a woman, were shot dead in separate incidents in District East earlier on Monday, police said, adding that the motives for the killings were unknown.
About 80 people have been killed in ethnic, political and sectarian violence in Karachi this year, compared to 500 last year and about 2,000 in 1995.
